blocks.title: Unit testing
blocks.text: Unit testing is testing the individual parts (units) of a program, such as single functions, separately to check that each works correctly.

Unit testing catches errors early and makes debugging easier. Python's modules automate testing of functions and methods, checking whether each component produces the expected output; clear, simple test cases improve reliability.

unittest is built into Python and provides a framework of test-case classes. pytest is an external module that makes tests simpler to write and run. Both verify that code behaves as expected, for single functions, classes or whole modules, and they improve stability in larger applications.

A test case gives a function specific inputs and states the expected output; for example, a calculator can be tested on addition and subtraction. Python runs the tests and reports any failures or errors. Running the tests again after every change shows that existing features still work, and automated running saves time.

blocks.title: Example: functions and their pytest tests (Python code; each .... is one 4-space indent)

items: pytest needs no test-case classes or extra boilerplate, unlike unittest: tests are plain functions.
assert checks whether the output is correct.
To run the tests, type pytest in the command line in the folder that holds the test file.
